newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. data propels Wall Street, Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. data propels Wall Street, Eurobourses.

text.p: European bourses were jolted higher along with Wall Street on Tuesday when benign inflation figures from Washington reduced the chances of an early rise in U.S. interest rates.
The Dow, which had lost nearly 200 points over the previous three sessions, opened 50 points higher and was up about 95 points, or nearly 1.5 percent, when European trading drew to a close.

The weaker-than-expected U.S. employment costs data, which sent U.S. Treasury bonds soaring, boosted London's blue chip FTSE 100 index which had previously been languishing in negative territory fearful that the global bull market was faltering.
In late afternoon trading the FTSE shook off its torpor and strode out of the red, closing more than half a percentage point up on the day.

It was a similar story in Frankfurt, where electronic trading closed well over one percent higher, and on the Paris bourse, where the blue chip CAC-40 index gained nearly two percent, scoring a record closing high above its previous all-time trading peak.
There was excitement too on currency markets, where the dollar continued its relentless climb, soaring past the psychological barrier of 121 yen on the back of the strong U.S. Treasury rally.

Earlier the dollar touched a 31-month high of 1.6569 marks before falling back slightly against the German currency. It was at around 1.6500 late in Europe -- still well over its late Monday European level of 1.6413 marks.
Financial markets had been anxiously awaiting the Employment Cost Index, which showed a smaller rise than Wall Street economists had been expecting.

The index was seen as key to any decision by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on interest rates at its meeting next week, especially after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warned of risks of wage-driven inflation in his testimony to the U.S. Senate Budget Committee last week.

"Today's U.S. Q4 employment cost index is one of the most important economic releases of the week, if not the year if it marks a possible turning point in Fed monetary policy," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in his daily outlook on Tuesday.

The U.S. Treasury bond rallied about a full percentage point immediately after the report was released, with the yield on the benchmark 30-year treasury bond falling to 6.85 percent from 6.94 percent late Monday.
Meanwhile, analysts said the dollar was also helped by reports that neither Germany nor Japan appeared very worried about the dollar's strength against their currencies.

The U.S. data and Wall Street's recovery came like a shot in the arm for European bourses, where investors had been fretting over the future direction of U.,S. markets with some fearing the Dow could be on the verge of a more substantial fall.

"The figure wasn't hugely better than expected but it has calmed nerves," a London trader said. "Some people were expecting a nasty figure and the one we got was inoffensive. A U.S. rate increase next week is now pretty unlikely."

In Frankfurt floor trading closed down before the U.S. data and Wall Street opened for business. But in post bourse electronic trading German shares took off, also boosted by the stronger dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.

In Paris the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 47.59 points or 1.95 percent at 2,482.76, breaking the old record of 2,461.25 set on January 23. The dollar's continued strong performance against European currencies also helped the bourse, French dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was at 121.20 yen and 1.6500 marks compared with late Europe's Monday level of 119.43 yen and 1.6413 marks.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 25.4 points higher at 4,237.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 47.59 at 2,482.76.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 5.20 at 2,989.33.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $353.10 compared with London's Monday close of $354.60. Silver closed at $4.98.
